name: dispatch_handler_from_table
description: Sets three fields of a request record (a length of 216, a zero status and the supplied pointer), makes three calls through the library jump table, then scans a 16-bit key table and jumps to the handler paired with the matching key.

name: fill_dos_packet_and_dispatch
description: Fills a nine-field record with fixed values, including a four-character tag that spells DOS, sets a status of minus one, makes three library calls, then scans a 16-bit key table and jumps to the matching handler.

name: copy_parent_directory_and_lookup
description: Copies the part of a path before its last slash into a length-prefixed local buffer and passes it to a lookup routine; the result pair is stored in the request record, zeros are stored when the path is empty, and control then dispatches through the key table.

name: clear_status_and_dispatch
description: Clears two result fields of a request record, stores the supplied pointer, makes two library calls, then scans the 16-bit key table and jumps to the handler paired with the matching key.

name: read_buffered_file_chunk
description: Copies the requested number of bytes out of a 30000-byte read buffer into the caller's destination, first from the cached window and then by refilling the buffer from the source, and reports the number of bytes delivered.

name: write_buffered_file_chunk
description: Appends bytes to a 30000-byte write buffer, growing the logical size and allocating the buffer on first use, and flushes through a library call when the buffer is full; the number of bytes written is reported back.

name: flush_write_buffer_and_return
description: Calls a flush routine through the library table, then records the requested byte count as the result and dispatches through the key table.

name: store_result_or_error_pair
description: Makes three calls; if the upper half of the 64-bit result is zero it stores the lower half in the request record, otherwise it stores a secondary value and an error status of minus one, then dispatches.

name: store_result_or_error_status
description: Makes five calls and stores the 64-bit result's lower half on success; on failure it stores a secondary value and minus one as the status, then dispatches through the key table.

name: retry_after_cleanup_and_store
description: Makes three routine calls and, when the 64-bit result has a nonzero upper half, calls a cleanup routine through the library table, repeats the three calls, and on a second failure stores the secondary value with an error status; on success it stores the first result with a zero status.

name: flush_pending_data_and_fail
description: Calls a flush routine when a pending-data field of the nested state record is nonzero, then sets the request status to minus one and dispatches through the key table.

name: seek_stream_position_within_size
description: Computes a target position from a base and an offset: the current position when the mode is zero, the total size when the mode is positive, or the bare offset otherwise. If the target lies past the total size it returns error 219; otherwise it moves the position there and returns the old one.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: shift_string_store_length
description: Shifts a null-terminated string one byte toward its end, moving its first character to position one, and stores the string's length without the terminator in the first byte.

name: allocate_init_record_or_free
description: Runs a setup routine and, if it succeeds, allocates a record block through the system library; a second setup call then fills four fields of the block with the setup result and three register values, and the block is returned. If that second call fails the block is freed and null is returned.

name: free_record_and_buffer
description: If given a non-null record, releases the data buffer it points to when one is present, then releases the record itself through the system library.

name: allocate_joined_path_string
description: Joins a directory string and a relative name into a newly allocated path, keeping text before a colon as the volume prefix, collapsing a trailing slash and resolving parent-directory components; on allocation failure it returns error 205.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: return_minus_one_constant
description: Returns the constant minus one and does nothing else; code takes its address, so it is used as a function pointer that reports a fixed failure value.

name: open_dos_library_and_patch
description: Opens dos.library through the Exec library vector table, then patches a library function vector with a replacement routine via SetFunction, and finishes with a call to another routine.

name: filter_result_code_values
description: Calls a routine through a stored pointer and returns its result, unless the result equals one of four specific codes, in which case it returns the original input value instead.

name: install_jump_hooks_if_marked
description: When a marker byte in the table entry is the letter d, it saves an existing word at a target slot, writes four absolute jump instructions that point at this module's routines, and then calls a routine; otherwise it returns without changes.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Makes one call to another routine and returns, with no other effect; its address is taken in code, so it acts as a pass-through entry point.

name: enable_interrupt_mask_intena
description: Calls another routine first, then writes the interrupt enable hardware register with the enable bit and the external interrupt bit set, which switches those interrupts on.

name: call_then_return_input_value
description: Calls another routine and returns the register value it was given, unchanged.

name: call_then_return_input_value
description: Calls another routine and returns the register value it was given, unchanged.

name: wait_forever_on_beam_position
description: Loops forever with no exit; the code reads the vertical beam position hardware register, so it is a wait loop that never returns, and the decompiled output keeps only the endless loop.

name: open_screen_at_entry
description: Entry code that opens the graphics and intuition libraries by name, sets a flag byte in a screen structure, calls a routine with a 640 by 256 size, and passes the stored handles on for further setup.

name: setup_graphics_screen_and_refresh
description: Opens the graphics and intuition libraries by name, sets a flag byte in a screen structure, calls a routine with a 640 by 256 size, and passes the stored handles to further routines.

name: clear_record_table_and_link
description: Zeroes a block of forty-two long words at an offset from a record pointer, stores the address of a stack buffer and a global value into two fields of that record, then calls another routine.

name: call_optional_hook_then_run
description: Calls a stored function pointer when it is set, then calls another routine and returns; the stored pointer is the optional hook.

name: split_text_into_token_array
description: Looks up two identifiers through library calls and, when the lookup succeeds, splits a text buffer at characters flagged in a class table, stores a pointer to each token in an allocated array terminated by a null pointer, and then makes further library calls.

name: run_setup_calls_and_return
description: Calls a routine ten times, then calls a stored function pointer and up to three stored-handle routines when they are set; it passes stored values to two routines and returns a call result or the input value depending on a stored flag.

name: append_string_with_limit
description: Appends the source string to the end of the destination, copying at most 32767 bytes and always writing a null terminator, then returns the destination pointer.

name: copy_string_with_limit
description: Finds the end of the destination string, then copies bytes from the source one by one, stopping at the first null byte or when the counter in the third argument runs out, and terminates the destination with a null byte.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies a null-terminated string into the destination, including its terminator, and returns the original destination pointer.

name: compute_string_length
description: Walks a null-terminated string until its terminator and returns the number of bytes before the terminator; it does not modify memory.

name: copy_bytes_with_padding
description: Copies bytes from the source for a counted length, stopping early at a zero byte, then fills the rest of the destination area for that count with zero bytes, and returns the destination pointer.

name: release_slot_if_loaded
description: Checks that a slot index falls within a 20-entry table and that the slot holds a value; if so it calls a library routine on the stored value unless a flag bit is set, clears the slot and returns zero. Invalid or empty slots set error code 3 and return minus one.

name: forward_call_via_library_base
description: Calls the function at library vector offset minus 414 of the library base pointer kept in a global slot, and returns.

name: open_library_via_stored_base
description: Calls the function at library vector offset minus 552 of the library base pointer kept in a global slot, and returns.

name: forward_call_via_second_base
description: Calls the function at library vector offset minus 384 of the library base pointer kept in a second global slot.

name: clear_state_and_start_program
description: Program entry: clears a block of 6794 long words of game state, saves the Exec base pointer, calls a routine when a bit in the Exec attention-flag word is set, then calls a routine and continues to one of two follow-on routines depending on its result.

name: update_status_byte_from_flags
description: Reads the processor's comparison flags; when the overflow and negative flags differ and carry is set, it returns the input byte OR-ed with a fixed constant, otherwise it stores a fixed constant in a global status byte and returns the input byte.

name: set_status_bit_two
description: Sets the bit with value 2 in a global status byte and returns.

name: read_button_flags_byte
description: Builds a result byte from a global input-state byte: 1 when the bit with value 64 is clear, plus 2 when the bit with value 4 is clear. The bits follow the fire and right or middle button readings described in the register notes.

name: set_state_to_seventy_nine
description: Stores the constant 79 into a global state byte and returns.

name: set_state_to_high_constant
description: Stores a fixed 16-bit-range constant into a global state byte and returns.

name: set_state_to_eight
description: Stores the constant 8 into a global state byte and returns.

name: update_pseudo_random_state
description: Advances a 32-bit state held in a global by doubling it and XOR-ing in a fixed feedback constant when the shift overflows. For a positive range argument it returns the state reduced modulo that range; otherwise it stores a negated seed and returns the input.

name: handle_keyboard_serial
description: When a flag bit is set, returns the complemented, rotated keyboard code byte, runs a fixed delay loop, and clears bit 64 of the state byte; otherwise it returns zero. The keyboard code is read from the keyboard serial register.

name: lookup_code_in_table
description: Reads a key code through a routine; when the code is nonzero and has no high bit set it scans a 49-entry table for that code and returns the paired value from a second table, or zero if it is not found.

name: copy_template_write_addresses
description: Copies a 180-word template into a buffer, then writes the high and low 16-bit parts of the parameter and of successive addresses spaced 8000 apart into fixed slots of that buffer.

name: write_fixed_structure_constants
description: Writes a fixed set of 16-bit constants at offsets from 142 up to 422 into a structure reached through a global pointer.

name: store_param_and_control_words
description: Writes a 32-bit parameter into one field of a structure, zeroes the 16-bit field beside it, and writes two 16-bit control words into a third field: 480 first, then 34784.

name: read_stored_pointer_value
description: Returns the 32-bit value held in a global pointer slot, without changing anything.

name: set_address_table_entries
description: Waits for the display beam to reach a raster line and then writes the high and low 16-bit parts of a second argument at addresses spaced 8000 apart in a table; the first argument is stored in a global slot when it is not minus one.

name: copy_sixteen_words_to_table
description: Copies sixteen 16-bit words from a source buffer into every other word slot of a table reached through a global pointer, starting at offset 114.

name: store_blit_parameters_then_wait
description: Stores eleven parameters into fixed fields of a structure reached through a global, packing one value as a low word plus 64 times a high word, then calls the blitter wait routine, which polls until the blitter is idle.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: invoke_three_setup_calls
description: Calls one routine with an address computed from a frame value, calls another with two sentinel values of minus one, then calls a third routine and returns.

name: lock_path_read_info_block
description: Locks a DOS name held in a global with read access, reads its information block into a global buffer, unlocks it, and returns the 32-bit word at offset four of that block; it returns zero when the lock fails.

name: lock_dh0_volume_read_info
description: Locks the DH0: volume through the DOS library with read access, reads its information block, unlocks it, and returns the low word of the field at offset four; it returns zero when the lock fails.

name: call_four_routines_unrecovered
description: No pseudo-code could be recovered, so this rests on the listed facts alone: a 43-instruction routine that calls four unnamed routines and one small negate-and-copy routine, with its behaviour otherwise unrecovered.

name: call_one_routine_unrecovered
description: No pseudo-code could be recovered, so this rests on the listed facts alone: a 22-instruction routine called by ten unnamed routines that makes one call to an unnamed routine, with its behaviour otherwise unrecovered.

name: initialise_tables_and_allocate_buffers
description: Allocates memory blocks of fixed sizes through the system library, clears several global tables in loops, releases entries from earlier lists, and calls routines to set up the display and raster-wait timing. Text references to the AUTO00.PRC script and the texte.dat data file show it also works with those resources.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_and_wait
description: Swaps two stored pointers in the global area, calls a routine with the new pointer, waits for the raster line, then writes one of two mode words into a structure field depending on the parameter, and calls another routine when a pending flag is set.

name: wait_raster_then_set_mode
description: Calls the raster wait routine and then stores a fixed mode word at offset 256 of a structure reached through a global pointer.

name: release_entries_and_reset_table
description: Loops over 255 entries of a table reached through a global; each non-empty entry is passed to a routine together with the product of two of its stored 16-bit values, then every entry is cleared with its two sentinel words set to minus one.

name: allocate_slot_for_block
description: Finds the first free entry among 255 table slots and, if one exists, allocates a block of width times height bytes, stores the size, one-eighth of the width, the height and a row count of four in the entry, sets two sentinel words and increments a count; it returns the slot index, or minus one when the table is full.

name: free_table_slot_block
description: Releases the block in a table slot when it is in use: it passes the stored size to a routine, clears the slot's fields, sets two sentinel words, calls a second routine on the slot's link field and decrements the count. An empty slot returns minus one.

name: repeat_call_count_times
description: Calls another routine once for each count given in its 16-bit argument, doing nothing else.

name: clear_two_global_longs
description: Stores zero into two 32-bit fields reached through a global base pointer and returns.

name: free_linked_list_nodes
description: Walks a linked list whose head pointer is kept in a global, passing each node and the size 20 to a routine, then calls a second routine.

name: insert_sorted_list_node
description: Walks a linked list whose head is kept in a global, comparing a 16-bit key looked up from a 32-byte table, allocates a 20-byte node, links it at the sorted position and copies two 16-bit fields from the parameter into it.

name: remove_list_node_by_key
description: Walks the list to find a node whose two 16-bit fields match the parameter; when found it unlinks that node, frees its 20-byte block and returns zero, otherwise it returns minus one.

name: clear_two_consecutive_globals
description: Stores zero into two consecutive 32-bit global slots and returns.

name: free_nodes_second_list
description: Walks a second linked list whose head is kept in a different global, passing each node and the size 20 to a routine, then calls a second routine.

name: append_table_row_node
description: Allocates a 20-byte node and links it at the end of the list whose head is kept in a global, copies the parameter's two 16-bit fields and four 16-bit values from a 32-byte table row into it, and records it as the head of a companion list.

name: insert_table_row_node
description: Allocates a 20-byte node and links it after the head given on the stack, copies two 16-bit fields from the stack arguments and four 16-bit values from a 32-byte table row into it, and updates the list head global.

name: clear_list_head_and_sentinel
description: Stores zero in a 32-bit global list head and sets a 16-bit flag global to minus one.

name: free_first_list_nodes
description: Walks the list whose head is kept in a global, passing each node and the size 214 to a routine, then calls a second routine.

name: append_record_node_to_tail
description: Walks to the tail of the list whose head is kept in a global, allocates a 214-byte node and links it at the end, copies a 50-word row from a table indexed by the parameter into it, clears a second 50-word block, and stores the index in the node.

name: mark_list_node_index_dead
description: Searches the list headed by a global for a node whose 16-bit index equals the argument; when found it sets that index to minus one and returns zero, otherwise it returns minus one.

name: remove_dead_list_nodes
description: Walks the list headed by a global and unlinks each node whose index is minus one, passing each unlinked node and the size 214 to a routine; the other nodes stay in place.

name: clear_second_list_head_sentinel
description: Stores zero in a 32-bit global list head and sets a different 16-bit flag global to minus one.

name: free_second_list_records
description: Walks the second list, whose head is kept in a global, passing each node and the size 214 to a routine, then calls a second routine.

name: append_record_node_and_process
description: Allocates a 214-byte node and appends it to the end of the second list, clears two 50-word blocks in it, stores a pointer from a table row chosen by the argument and the index, then passes that stored pointer and the node's inner block to a further routine.

name: mark_second_list_node_removed
description: Searches the second list for a node whose index equals the argument; when found it sets that index to minus one and returns zero, otherwise it returns minus one.

name: remove_dead_second_list_nodes
description: Walks the second list and unlinks each node whose index is minus one, passing each unlinked node and the size 214 to a routine.

name: dispatch_slot_with_row_values
description: Reads four 16-bit values from a 32-byte table row and a slot index; when the slot holds a pointer it calls a routine with that pointer and the row values, choosing an argument set from a flag word, then calls a routine with zero.

name: dispatch_stack_slot_values
description: Calls a routine with the pointer of a slot indexed by a stack value, together with two stack-held 16-bit values and a masked combination, then calls another routine with zero.

name: store_parameters_and_computed_offsets
description: Copies four 16-bit parts of two arguments into separate global words, then computes two more: the first argument's low word times eight plus its high word times 160, and 160 minus the second argument's low word times eight.

name: call_with_two_stored_pointers
description: Calls another routine once with two pointers loaded from global slots and returns.

name: branch_on_stored_coordinate_match
description: Compares three stored 16-bit values with zero, 160 and 200; when all match it calls one routine twice with two stored pointers, otherwise it calls that routine twice with additional stored arguments.

name: call_twice_with_stored_pointers
description: Calls another routine twice, each time with a different stored pointer, together with a shared stored 16-bit value and a register value.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: set_table_field_by_kind
description: Writes a 16-bit argument into one of six fields of a 32-byte table entry, chosen by a kind value in the second argument: kind three also calls a routine and, when it returns zero, calls another; kind five substitutes a stored default for minus one.

name: store_table_entry_field_one
description: Writes a 16-bit value from a stack argument into the first field of a 32-byte table entry indexed by another stack argument.

name: store_table_entry_field_six
description: Writes a 16-bit value from a stack argument into the sixth field of a 32-byte table entry indexed by another stack argument.

name: store_table_entry_four_fields
description: Writes four 16-bit values into the first four fields of a 32-byte table entry indexed by the first argument, then calls a routine and calls another when it returns zero.

name: read_four_word_bit_mask
description: Computes an address from its arguments, reads four consecutive 16-bit words, tests one bit position in each (the position comes from the low nibble of the first argument), and returns a four-bit mask built from those tests.

name: test_bit_in_table_word
description: Computes an index from its arguments, reads a 16-bit table value at that index, and returns whether the bit selected by the low nibble of the first argument is set.

name: run_main_loop_until_exit
description: Initialises table and display state, runs a frame loop of input and redraw calls, and refers to the exit text Tout est Ok . Bye.

name: process_button_input_and_dialog
description: Reads input bits through a routine and accumulates button flags over up to 100 reads; it then branches on a state word and calls many routines that update display and entry state in the structure referenced by a global.

name: process_selection_state_switch
description: When a state word is zero, fills stack buffers through several routine calls, repeats a call while a counter is nonzero, then switches on the result of a table lookup; the cases make further lookups and update a stored selection index and a flag byte.

name: find_entry_matching_fields
description: Scans up to 255 twelve-byte entries of a table reached through a global for one whose occupied flag is set and whose 16-bit fields match the first argument and the second argument's first word, with a second word also compared when the kind is two; it returns the entry index or minus one.

name: find_entry_at_position
description: Walks a list of entries from a global head and returns the index of the first active entry whose stored region contains the point given in the argument, using a size from a shape table; for two kinds of entry it calls a test routine. It returns minus one when nothing matches.

name: draw_entry_list_frame
description: Clears a region, then walks the entry list from a global head: entries of kind zero are passed to a drawing routine with coordinate and shape-table arguments, while kind-two entries are handled by separate routine calls.

name: render_kind_five_entries_buffered
description: Walks a list of entries; for each entry of kind five it passes the entry's shape and position to a routine, allocating a temporary buffer once for the first such entry, then finishes with that buffer, or passes the original arguments to a routine when no entry matched.

name: render_kind_five_entries_masked
description: Walks a list of entries; for each entry of kind five it allocates a temporary buffer once and passes the entry's shape and position with a masking argument to a routine, then finishes with that buffer, or calls the routine with the original arguments when no entry matched.

name: visit_each_list_node
description: Walks the list headed by a global, calling a routine with each node in turn.

name: visit_second_list_nodes
description: Walks the list headed by a different global, calling a routine with each node in turn.

name: interpret_script_opcodes
description: Steps through an opcode stream stored in a structure, dispatching each opcode to a routine or to a routine that writes a returned value into a table, and advances the stream position until a stop flag is set.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_a
description: Reads script opcodes from a stream and dispatches them; one path reads three bytes and passes a 16-bit value to a routine, opcode two writes a routine result into a table, and opcodes three and four call further routines.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_b
description: Reads script opcodes from a stream and dispatches them: the entry path reads two bytes and passes a 16-bit value to a routine, opcode two writes a routine result into a table, and opcode three calls a further routine.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_c
description: Reads script opcodes from a stream: the entry path reads eight bytes and passes two 16-bit values to a routine, and the dispatch switch then handles further opcodes through routine calls, including a table write.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_d
description: Script opcode that reads a 16-bit pair of operands and passes them to a routine, then consumes nine bytes of stream; it dispatches further opcodes through a switch, with table writes and routine calls among the cases.

name: apply_script_table_assignment
description: Script opcode that writes a value into a slot of the main 16-bit table: mode zero stores a literal, mode one copies another slot, mode two copies from a secondary array, and mode five stores the absolute value of a routine's result.

name: add_to_script_table_slot
description: Script opcode that adds to a slot of the main 16-bit table: mode zero adds a literal, and other modes add the value of another slot.

name: subtract_from_script_table_slot
description: Script opcode that subtracts from a slot of the main 16-bit table: mode zero subtracts a literal, and other modes subtract the value of another slot.

name: multiply_script_table_slot
description: Script opcode that multiplies a slot of the main 16-bit table by a literal or by the value of another slot.

name: divide_script_table_slot
description: Script opcode that divides a slot of the main 16-bit table by a literal or by the value of another slot.

name: divide_table_slot_by_literal
description: Script opcode that divides a slot of the main 16-bit table by a 16-bit literal read from the stream.

name: store_routine_result_from_table
description: Script opcode that calls a routine with a literal or with a table slot's value and stores the returned 16-bit result in a fixed field of the state structure.

name: store_side_table_value
description: Script opcode that writes a literal, or the value of a main-table slot, into a slot of a secondary 16-bit array; mode two copies from that secondary array instead.

name: store_routine_result_from_operand
description: Script opcode that calls a routine with a literal, a main-table slot value or a secondary-array value, and stores the returned 16-bit result in a fixed field of the state structure.

name: call_routine_with_zero_op
description: Script opcode that reads one byte into a temporary slot and calls a routine with zero, then continues dispatching the stream.

name: call_routine_with_five_op
description: Script opcode that reads one byte into a temporary slot and calls a routine with five, then continues dispatching the stream.

name: store_byte_in_control_field
description: Script opcode that stores one operand byte into a 16-bit control field of the state structure.

name: call_routine_with_zero_op
description: Script opcode that reads one byte into a temporary slot and calls a routine with zero, then continues dispatching the stream.

name: run_three_routine_calls_op
description: Script opcode that reads one byte and makes three routine calls, the first of them through a library vector, then continues dispatching the stream.

name: call_routine_with_one_op
description: Script opcode that reads one byte into a temporary slot and calls a routine with one, then continues dispatching the stream.

name: record_script_label_position
description: Script opcode that stores the current stream position plus one in a label table, at the index given by the operand byte.

name: clear_script_label_slot
description: Script opcode that sets one entry of the script label table to minus one, at the index given by the operand byte.

name: jump_to_script_label
description: Script opcode that moves the stream position to the label stored at the index given by the operand byte.

name: branch_on_flag_bits_two
description: Script opcode that jumps to a label-table entry when state flag bit value 2 is set and bit value 1 is clear; otherwise it moves past the operand byte.

name: branch_on_flag_bits_either
description: Script opcode that jumps to a label-table entry when state flag bit value 2 or bit value 1 is set; otherwise it moves past the operand byte.

name: branch_on_flag_bit_four
description: Script opcode that jumps to a label-table entry when state flag bit value 4 is set and bit value 1 is clear; otherwise it moves past the operand byte.

name: jump_if_bit_one_set
description: Script opcode that jumps to a label-table entry when state flag bit value 1 is set; otherwise it moves past the operand byte.

name: jump_if_bit_one_clear
description: Script opcode that jumps to a label-table entry when state flag bit value 1 is clear; otherwise it moves past the operand byte.

name: decrement_and_loop_script_counter
description: Script opcode that decrements a counter slot and jumps to a label-table entry while the counter is still non-negative; otherwise it moves past the operand bytes.

name: call_routine_with_operand_byte
description: Script opcode that reads a byte operand from the stream and passes it to a routine, then advances the stream by two bytes.

name: call_routine_then_skip_byte
description: Script opcode that calls a routine with no operand, then advances the stream past one operand byte.

name: call_routine_then_skip_byte
description: Script opcode that calls a routine with no operand, then advances the stream past one operand byte.

name: copy_string_operand_and_call
description: Script opcode that copies a zero-terminated string from the stream into a local buffer, passes that buffer to a routine and makes further library calls.

name: load_animation_from_string
description: Script opcode that copies a zero-terminated name from the stream and passes it to an animation loader; on failure it sets a status flag and reports the error text 'ECHEC LoadAni' with the name.

name: set_script_string_for_slot
description: Script opcode that reads a slot index and a zero-terminated string from the stream, then passes the string with the address of that slot to a routine.

name: load_background_from_string
description: Script opcode that copies a zero-terminated name from the stream and passes it to a background loader; on failure it sets a status flag and reports the error text 'ECHEC LoadBg' with the name.

name: load_named_resource_from_string
description: Script opcode that copies a zero-terminated name from the stream and passes it to a loader; on failure it sets a status flag and calls a reporting routine with the name, then continues dispatching.

name: load_ct_resource_or_report
description: Script opcode that copies a zero-terminated name from the stream and passes it to a loader; on failure it sets a status flag and reports the error text 'ECHEC LoadCt' with the name, then continues dispatching.

name: run_three_setup_routines
description: Script opcode that makes three routine calls, the first through a library vector, and then continues dispatching script opcodes.

name: call_routine_then_dispatch
description: Script opcode that calls a routine once and then continues dispatching script opcodes.

name: set_script_flag_one
description: Script opcode that sets a 16-bit state word to one and then continues dispatching script opcodes.

name: pause_script_at_position
description: Script opcode that saves the current stream position in the script state and sets the stop flag, which ends the dispatch loop.

name: set_mode_flag_one
description: Script opcode that sets a mode word to one and then continues dispatching script opcodes.

name: set_mode_flag_zero
description: Script opcode that sets a mode word to zero and then continues dispatching script opcodes.

name: run_branch_then_stop
description: Calls one of two routines depending on a state field, then sets the stop flag so the script dispatch loop ends.

name: set_pending_word_one
description: Sets a 16-bit state word to one and then continues dispatching script opcodes.

name: call_routine_with_five_operands
description: Script opcode that reads five operands from the stream, one byte and four 16-bit values, passes them to a routine, and then continues dispatching script opcodes.

name: measure_script_opcode_stream
description: Clears a 50-entry table to minus one, then steps through an opcode stream, advancing by the operand length of each opcode from a switch on the opcode value, until the end of the stream is reached.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_f
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads one byte and a 16-bit operand from the stream, passes the operand to a routine, and then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_g
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads three operand bytes from the stream, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_f
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads one byte and a 16-bit operand from the stream, passes the operand to a routine, and then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_h
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads nine operand bytes, one byte and four 16-bit values, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_i
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads a byte and then either a single byte or a 16-bit operand, depending on a second operand byte, before dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_j
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads one operand byte from the stream, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: store_script_position_in_table
description: Script opcode that stores the current stream position plus one in a table reached through the state structure, at the index given by the operand byte.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_j
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads one operand byte from the stream, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_l
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads two operand bytes from the stream, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_j
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads one operand byte from the stream, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_m
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads one byte and a 16-bit operand from the stream, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: read_string_operand_then_dispatch
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads one operand byte and then a zero-terminated string from the stream, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: resume_script_dispatch_loop
description: Enters the script opcode dispatcher with no operand, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: end_script_dispatch
description: Sets the stop flag in the script state, which ends the dispatch loop.

name: resume_script_dispatch_loop
description: Enters the script opcode dispatcher with no operand, then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: dispatch_script_opcodes_entry_o
description: Entry to the script opcode dispatcher that reads eight operand bytes, arranged as four 16-bit values, and then continues dispatching the remaining opcodes.

name: compare_word_halves_flags
description: Compares the low and high 16-bit halves of its 32-bit argument and returns a flag byte: bit value 1 when they are equal, bit value 2 when the high half is less than the low half, and bit value 4 when the low half is less than the high half.

name: blit_shifted_rows_clipped
description: Draws a graphic row by row into a buffer, using the low nibble of the horizontal position as a bit shift and the remaining bits as a word offset, and clipping the horizontal position against a range of 160; it uses three routine calls for setup and output.

name: return_parameter_unchanged
description: Returns the single 64-bit parameter it receives without change and makes no calls.

name: blit_shifted_rows_variant
description: Draws a graphic row by row with the same bit-shift and word-offset arithmetic as its neighbours, clipping the horizontal position against 160, and makes three routine calls to set up and output the rows.

name: return_parameter_unchanged
description: Returns the single 64-bit parameter it receives without change and makes no calls.

name: blit_shifted_rows_simple
description: Draws a graphic row by row with the same bit-shift and word-offset arithmetic as its neighbours, clipping the horizontal position against 160 and making three routine calls to set up and output the rows.

name: return_parameter_unchanged
description: Returns the single 64-bit parameter it receives without change and makes no calls.

name: call_blit_setup_fixed_size
description: Calls a blit setup routine once with the argument, a mask of 65535 and a fixed size of 800, and returns.

name: configure_four_plane_blits
description: Calls a blit setup routine four times with the same fixed arguments, advancing the base address by 8000 each time and using a height of 200.

name: stub_return_no_effect
description: A three-instruction routine with no body: it only returns, so calls to it have no effect in the recovered code.

name: call_four_planes_masked
description: Reads a base address from a global, converts four bits of the third argument into four 16-bit masks, and calls a routine four times with the base advanced by 8000 each time and those masks.

name: configure_four_blit_blocks
description: Computes a width and height from two coordinate pairs, obtains a base offset through a routine, and builds four blit parameter blocks whose masks come from the flag bits of the third argument, calling routines to program them.

name: configure_blit_from_rect
description: Computes a width, height and base address from two coordinate pairs and a global base pointer, then calls a blit setup routine once with those derived values.

name: call_single_routine_unrecovered
description: No pseudo-code could be recovered, so this rests on the listed facts alone: a 76-instruction routine that makes one call to an unnamed routine, with its behaviour otherwise unrecovered.

name: process_text_entry_from_table
description: Looks up a text byte string in a table of six-byte entries indexed by the first argument; an empty entry sets an error code, otherwise the string is measured, the stored position is advanced by its length, and seven routine calls lay it out.

name: clear_shifted_mask_rows
description: Repeats eight times: reads 16-bit words from a source pointer, shifts them by the low nibble of the third argument, combines the shifted parts, and clears the matching bits in destination rows spaced 40 bytes apart.

name: call_several_routines_unrecovered
description: No pseudo-code could be recovered, so this rests on the listed facts alone: an 81-instruction routine called by four unnamed routines, with its behaviour otherwise unrecovered.

name: append_node_to_main_list
description: Allocates a 20-byte node, links it at the end of the list whose head is kept in a global, and stores a type value of two with the two 16-bit parameter fields in it.

name: insert_node_after_stack_pointer
description: Allocates a 20-byte node, links it into the list after the node given on the stack, and stores a type value of two with four 16-bit fields taken from the stack.

name: prepend_typed_node_to_list
description: Walks to the end of the list headed by a global, allocates a 20-byte node, stores a type value of three and the parameter in it, and links it at the head of a companion list.
